extra.WP-44:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [CR 85 from WP-16] Lead decision: the tlsconf row of 1.2 stays 'secret, errcode' (no v1alpha1), so the v1alpha1-typed signatures that spec 06 section 3 sketches are not built. Listener certificates become `[]tlsconf.CertSpec{Name, Certificate: secret.RefOf(c.Certificate), PrivateKey: secret.RefOf(c.PrivateKey)}` for `tlsconf.BuildCertIndex(specs, store)`, then `tlsconf.NewListenerState(tlsconf.ListenerOptions{MinVersion, Certs, RequestClientCert})`; the snapshot compiler does this conversion. Upstream.spec.tls and telemetry.otlp.tls become `tlsconf.ClientSpec{SNI, CACertificate, ClientCertificate, ClientKey *secret.Ref}` for `tlsconf.Upstream(spec, store)` and `tlsconf.OTLP(&spec, store)` (nil spec: system roots). The owner calls Close on the CertIndex or ClientConfig when it retires it, which stops its secret watches.
- [CR 89 from WP-16] tlsconf.ServerOptions has only State, and the tlsconf.Server configuration does not observe handshakes: crypto/tls has no post-handshake hook, and VerifyConnection runs before the client's last flight. Measure spec 06 req 77 around the listener's own (*tls.Conn).HandshakeContext call: a nil error observes ruralz_listener_tls_handshake_duration_seconds from accept, and an error counts ruralz_listener_connections_total{result='tls_failure'}. On the Go 1.26 floor, net/http handshakes a *tls.Conn itself with no completion hook, so complete the handshake (bounded by the listener's handshake timeout) before handing the *tls.Conn to http.Server, which then skips its own. Do this per connection off the Accept loop, on goroutines the listener owns and bounds by the connection ceiling, so a slow client cannot stall accepts. Build tls.Server over the connection wrapper that implements tlsconf.ClientCertRecorder, so GetConfigForClient can record the request mode on the NetConn chain.
- [CR 4 from WP-15] clientaddr.ListenerOptions.Clock must track wall time, because Clock.Now()+Timeout goes to net.Conn.SetReadDeadline, which the OS enforces against the real clock. A fake seeded at a fixed date refuses every PROXY connection at once, or never times out. Production passes clock.Real() (WP-76 wiring); tests pass clock.Real() or clocktest.New(clock.Real().Now()). The gateway/listener row in 1.2 does not list clock, so take a clientaddr.TimeSource (clock.Clock satisfies it) through the listener's options instead of importing clock.
extra.WP-45:
Notes from the wave-2 boundary: contract change requests forwarded to this work package, with the lead's decisions. The architecture and wps.json already reflect the decisions; these notes give detail.
- [Decision 2026-10-09, OQ-data-plane-18 (b)] Admin 404 and 405 problem documents carry codes: any path outside the admin table is 404 RZ-RT-020 ("No admin endpoint") and any other method on a known path is 405 RZ-RT-021 ("Method not allowed on admin endpoint"), both registered in internal/errcode with titles in internal/problem. Build them with internal/problem like every other admin error (never a bare net/http 404 or an empty code), set Allow on the 405, answer 404 and 405 only after adminauth admits the request (an unknown path without an admitted operator credential stays 401, internal/adminauth/adminauth.go:13-19), treat HEAD as another method (a ServeMux "GET /x" pattern also matches HEAD, and the admin table lists GET only), and test both on every admin path and method.
